blogTitle: Color Matching Guide for Wall Art - How to Choose Perfect Colours?
videoTitle: How Do You Choose Wall Art Colours That Actually Work?
script:
How Do You Choose Wall Art Colours That Actually Work?

Choosing wall art colours that complement your space can feel overwhelming — but it really doesn't have to be.

Should the art match your walls? Contrast with them? Pull from your accent colours?

The truth is, there's no single right answer — but there are proven strategies that make it much easier.

Understanding how colours interact gives you the confidence to make choices you'll love for years.

The colour wheel is your essential tool. It organises colours by their relationships — primary, secondary, and tertiary.

Primary colours — red, blue, yellow — combine to create secondary colours like orange, green, and purple.

Secondary colours mix with primaries to form tertiary colours — those lovely in-between shades.

Complementary colours sit opposite each other on the wheel — they create bold, lively contrast.

Analogous colours sit next to each other on the wheel — they feel harmonious and soothing together.

A little tip I love: pull one colour from your existing soft furnishings and use it to anchor your art choice.

This set of 3 Japanese Sunset prints works beautifully in monochrome rooms — the contrast does all the work.

Matching art to your wall colour? Try pulling the exact wall tone as a neutral background in the art.

Contrasting art against your walls creates a focal point — especially effective in neutral rooms.

These abstract framed prints in a set of 2 add a confident pop of colour to any neutral living room wall.

Take care not to choose art colours based on photos alone — always check swatches in your actual room light.

Natural light changes throughout the day — what looks warm at noon can feel cool by evening.

If you're forgetful like me, keep a photo of your room's colour palette on your phone when you're shopping.

These Moroccan-inspired prints bring rich warm tones — my favourite style for adding depth to a plain wall.

Tonal colour schemes — different shades of one colour — feel calm and very easy to live with.

Bold contrast works too — a dark art piece against a white wall is one of the most timeless combinations.

This set of 3 living room art prints works across a wide range of colour schemes — a very versatile choice.

When choosing art for a colourful room, look for a print that contains at least one of your existing accent colours.

Cooler-toned rooms — blue, grey, green — pair well with art in similar muted, cool palettes.

Warmer rooms — terracotta, ochre, blush — suit art with earthy or warm tonal palettes beautifully.

These set-of-3 Chinese-inspired art prints bring elegant warm neutrals — beautiful against both dark and light walls.

A quick rule of thumb: your art doesn't have to match everything — it just needs to belong in the room.

For galleries or sets, keep a consistent palette across all pieces so the group reads as one cohesive display.

These modern living room prints in a set of 3 are designed to work as a cohesive group right out of the box.

Still unsure? Start with a neutral print and layer colour through your soft furnishings instead.

Choosing wall art colours is really just about listening to the room you already have.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
